title: Engineering Operations Technician, RNO101
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.
NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Physical Requirements:
• Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
• Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
• Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
• Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
• Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection
This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
• Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
• Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
• Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility
Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.


Key job responsibilities
• Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
• Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
• Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
• Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
• Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
• Technical writing to support change management program
• Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
• On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
• Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
• Role may support more than one location/site.


A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of electrical or mechanical, or 1+ years of data center or mission critical facilities (example: hospital, military facility, public safety facility, etc.) experience
- 1+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work a flexible work schedule including evenings, overnights, and weekends

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- 1+ years of relevant technical position, or 6+ months of professional or military experience
- Associate's degree in related field, or technical degree in related field

descriptionHtml:
Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

The Project Engineer - Ground Support Equipment is the technical expert in design and operation of launch site ground support equipment (GSE). This role interfaces directly with launch site engineers and management to understand GSE needs for new and existing processing facilities. Additionally, the Mechanical Project Engineer - Ground Support Equipment will develop cost estimations, lead procurement, manage vendors, run design reviews, and establish acceptance criteria for maintaining and commission hardware. This position is responsible for designs and managing all phases for new and existing ground support equipment in support of Leo launch operations.

The ideal candidate is comfortable in a highly technical setting and leads collaboration with other departments to reach the best solution to any problem. The candidate will have extensive experience with mechanical, pneumatic and electrical system development for GSE, with particular focus on satellite processing.

Key job responsibilities
• Design and manage GSE through development and build cycles to support launch operations.
• Coordinate with launch operations personnel to understand operational requirements and develop GSE to meet those requirements.
• Develop and approve specifications for performance, fabrication, acceptance test and maintenance.
• Manage external partners to ensure GSE meets specifications and timelines.
• Establish technical documentation for maintenance and proofload requirements.
• Perform analysis (hand calculations and finite element analysis) to support design.
• Design and analysis of concept CAD models using Siemens NX and Femap.
• Maintain and report on equipment schedule, budget, and technical status.
• Implement and continuously improve GSE operations.
• Assembly, integration, and test takt time and cost optimization planning.
• Shift schedule will vary, depending on production/launch schedules
• Must be willing and able to perform extended travel up to 25% annually, either domestically or internationally as business needs demand.
• Must be able to pass Kennedy Space Center background checks and maintain ongoing facility access.

A day in the life
The GSE Engineer will spend significant amounts of time collaborating with engineering, quality, and manufacturing teams to determine GSE needs. They will be responsible for maintaining hardware to support operations. They will lead GSE efforts at the launch sites and address root cause of failures and issues, implement corrective actions and hardware modifications.

We are a fast-paced, data-driven team, and work with leaders in multiple technology areas to deliver the best product for our customers. We hold each other to relentlessly high standards, and constantly look for ways to improve the product’s performance, quality and cost. We are excited about the technical challenges, which motivates us rather than discourages us. We dive deep to find root cause and implement solutions to ensure long term reliability.

We want individuals who are ready for this challenge and want to reach beyond what is possible today.

Amazon’s culture of inclusion is reinforced within our 16 Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.

At Amazon, our mission is to be the most customer-centric company on Earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright and driven people. We're dedicated to supporting new team members. Our team has a broad mix of experience levels and Amazon tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship.

- Experience with prototyping and implementation
- 2+ years of experience of structural analysis including hand calculations and Finite Element Analysis

From coaching leadership teams on workforce and talent management to driving HR process excellence, you'll collaborate with business leaders to develop forward-looking strategies focused on operational objectives and team effectiveness. Success in this role comes from your ability to navigate organizational dynamics, lead change initiatives, and make high-judgment decisions in ambiguous situations. title: Engineering Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work a flexible work schedule including evenings, overnights, and weekends
- 1+ years of electrical facilities maintenance, or 1+ years of mechanical facilities

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- Associate's degree in related field, or technical degree in related field

descriptionHtml:

title: Security Engineer II, Stores AppSec
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s Stores AppSec Team is seeking a Security Engineer to help keep Amazon secure for its customers. In this role, you will attack Amazon’s services, applications, and websites to discover security issues and report them to our internal technology teams. This position will provide you with challenging opportunities, both technologically and as a leader, but will also be a great deal of fun if hacking Amazon alongside a team of highly skilled individuals sounds exciting to you.

A Security Engineer at Amazon is expected to be strong in multiple domains. Engineers in this role work closely with teams throughout Information Security, as well as provide technical leadership and advice to teams and leaders throughout Amazon.

You will be in direct contact with teams in a variety of business verticals, giving you first hand knowledge about how Amazon is built and how it operates at a deep, technical level. Additionally, you will leverage the knowledge you gain about Amazon to find new ways to break services, processes, and technologies throughout the company. Engineers in this role must show exemplary judgment in making technical trade-offs between short-term fixes and long-term security and business goals.

You will demonstrate resilience and navigate ambiguous situations with composure and tact. You will be expected to provide thought leadership for the organization as you discover, invent, and innovate throughout the course of your duties. Above all else, a strong sense of customer obsession is necessary to focus on the ultimate goal of keeping Amazon and its customers secure.


Key job responsibilities
Your team has an emphasis on fast paced, highly visible engagements. You will be comfortable with a high level of ambiguity, exercising strong ownership, and be able to make high judgement decisions focusing on what is best for Amazon's Customers. Additionally, you should thrive in navigating complex stakeholder engagements a skill integral to the teams success.

In this role, you will primarily be:
- Conducting high quality application security reviews and penetration tests independently, or as part of a team
- Creating detailed engagement plans and thoroughly documenting findings, gaps, and remediation recommendations
- Contributing to team tooling, innovation, and improvements
- Communicating and collaborating with partner teams, service owners, Information Security, and senior leadership to influence, prioritize, and drive the resolution of discovered security findings

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

- 3+ years of programming in Python, Ruby, Go, Swift, Java, .Net, C++ or similar object oriented language experience

- 2+ years of troubleshooting systems issues, analyzing logs, or automating basic tasks using command line tools (non-internship) experience
- Bachelor's degree in a STEM field (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics), or 2+ years of IT Security experience
- Knowledge of networking protocols such as HTTP, DNS and TCP/IP
- Knowledge of industry-based security vulnerabilities and remediation techniques

title: Network Development Engineer , Wireless and Access, Network Access Technologies
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon's Network Access Technology team and build automation that keeps the world's largest enterprise wireless network running and healing itself. You'll design and deploy next-generation access infrastructure across thousands of global sites, solving complex problems at massive scale while your work directly enables every package Amazon delivers.

Your primary focus is building automation that makes our global wireless network self-sufficient and resilient. You'll analyze patterns across thousands of sites, develop workflows that resolve issues without human intervention, and validate new hardware before it reaches production environments.

You partner with firmware, field operations, and infrastructure engineers—pressure-testing designs and influencing decisions through data-driven insights. You'll mentor newer engineers, conduct technical reviews, and occasionally visit sites for hands-on validation and troubleshooting.

No two weeks look the same, but the constant is this: you're solving complex problems at unprecedented scale, and your work directly impacts the reliability of our fulfillment network worldwide.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and Deploy Network Solutions: Lead the design, development, and deployment of network access solutions spanning wireless (Wi-Fi 5/6/6E/7), wired (802.1X, NAC), and emerging network access technologies across Amazon's global fulfillment network.
- Own End-to-End Project Delivery: Take ownership of complex, multi-milestone network engineering projects from requirements gathering through deployment and validation, ensuring alignment with internal processes and stakeholder expectations.
- Build Automation and Tooling: Develop and enhance automation frameworks for network configuration, compliance validation, and zero-touch deployment pipelines that reduce manual effort and improve consistency.
- Enable Self-Healing Operations: Contribute to our automation platform by developing automated remediation workflows, anomaly detection models, and predictive maintenance capabilities for wireless infrastructure.
- Drive Cross-Team Collaboration: Partner with engineering, field operations, network operations, and program management teams to develop solutions that balance performance, cost, and operational simplicity while validating new device types and configurations.

A day in the life
You start on a design you own: whether 6E SSIDs can go fleet-wide without breaking specific clients, which means a staged rollout and systematic metric validation built into the deployment. Midday an escalation lands, and you help troubleshoot wireless performance for real time applications in the Fulfillment Center. In the afternoon you write the one-page recommendation to your director on standardizing the next generation of fulfillment centers on a single wireless platform, with cost, operational load, and migration risk laid out plainly enough that a decision can actually be made.

Amazon offers a full range of benefits to support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. 1. Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage

About the team
The NAT team's mission is to provide highly available network connectivity to all Amazon Operations clients. We work to make it easy to onboard critical use cases to the network and ensure that our network capacity meets the customer demand.

In order to achieve these goals we take an automation first approach with our Netfix automation platform.

We use AI to analyze trends and provide initial support for customer requests. We use data learned from AI to improve our processes and automation.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience

- 8+ years of experience with major internet routing protocols; specifically, BGP, OSPF, MPLS, RSVP and ISIS in a large enterprise environment.
- 8+ years working with major network operating systems such as Cisco IOS and/ or Junos.
- 3+ years experience with Unix/Linux

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of analog or RF layout design experience
- A Masters in Computer Science, MBA, or equivalent experience.
- Expert-level certifications (e.g. CCIE, JNCIE) a plus.
- Expert-level scripting and or automation skills in a network environment.

You will be responsible for managing a group of technicians who are installing and building server rack capacity for our customers. You must be passionate about Customer Experience, think and act globally and want to contribute to innovations in Data Center Infrastructure.

title: Mistrz utrzymania ruchu i infrastruktury
descriptionHtml:
Nasz zespół ds. utrzymania ruchu i infrastruktury jest centralnym ogniwem zaangażowania firmy Amazon w innowacyjność. W miarę rozwoju i przystosowania się firmy Amazon do ciągłych zmian, zespół ten dba o to, aby wykorzystywane przez nas narzędzia i technologie również szły z duchem czasu. Mistrz utrzymania ruchu i infrastruktury pomaga nam być zawsze o krok do przodu, wdrażając najnowsze technologie i identyfikując nowe, wydajne sposoby pracy. Zwraca szczególną uwagę na nasze procesy, aby pomóc utrzymać wysokie standardy, a także wprowadza ulepszenia, aby podnieść je jeszcze wyżej.

Key job responsibilities
Obowiązki

- Modelowanie najlepszych praktyk w zakresie bezpiecznego użytkowania sprzętu i monitorowanie zespołów w celu zapewnienia, że wszyscy przestrzegają właściwych procesów
- Śledzenie wydajności sprzętu poprzez kontrole wizualne, monitorowanie stanu technicznego i zadania związane z konserwacją zapobiegawczą oraz, w razie potrzeby, planowanie dodatkowych czynności serwisowych
- Nadzorowanie techników na zmianie w celu wspierania ich rozwoju i pełnienie roli pierwszego punktu kontaktu dla inżynierów utrzymania ruchu i infrastruktury
- Rozwiązywanie problemów związanych z urządzeniami w celu ograniczenia przestojów w pracy, umożliwiając jak najszybszą obsługę paczek
- Udział w poszukiwaniu sposobów ciągłego usprawnienia systemów i standaryzacji procesów w całej sieci europejskiej

Co oferujemy:
W Amazon wiemy, że każdy jest inny – dlatego oferujemy szereg fantastycznych benefitów dla Ciebie i Twojej rodziny:
- Prywatna opieka zdrowotna
- Ubezpieczenie na życie
- Program Wsparcia Pracowników
- Wsparcie w zakładaniu rodziny
- Karta MultiSport
- Opieka rodzinna
- Kod zniżki pracowniczej
- Obiady za 1zł
- Treningi i szkolenia wewnętrzne w dziale Utrzymania Ruchu
- Dostęp do platformy etutor




A day in the life
Dzień z życia

Osoba na tym stanowisku zarządza zespołem na swojej zmianie, upewniając się, że odpowiedni sprzęt jest dla każdego dostępny i że działa prawidłowo. Obejmuje to monitorowanie procesów w celu zapewnienia przestrzegania przepisów i zasad oraz zagwarantowanie, że przeprowadzana jest konserwacja zapobiegawcza w celu zwiększenia niezawodności sprzętu.
Biorąc pod uwagę wszystko, co obserwuje podczas swojej pracy, przedstawia sugestie dotyczące ulepszeń, aby nasze systemy były bardziej wydajne i produktywne, a następnie wdraża je w obrębie całej UE. Monitoruje również procesy za pomocą narzędzi takich jak Scada, aby zagwarantować ich wydajność, a także ściśle współpracuje ze swoim bezpośrednim przełożonym, pomagając w zadaniach administracyjnych.
Osoba na tym stanowisku pracuje w jednym z naszych centrów logistycznych w systemie zmianowym, który obejmuje niektóre weekendy oraz pracę nocną. W miarę rozwoju doświadczenia w tym ekscytującym segmencie firmy Amazon otrzyma dobre przygotowanie do awansu na wyższe stanowiska.

About the team
Informacje o zespole

Centrum logistyczne to miejsce, w którym firma Amazon stawiała swoje pierwsze kroki. Ze skromnego zespołu sprzedawców książek przekształciło się ono w wysokorozwiniętą korporację o zasięgu ogólnoświatowym, która każdego dnia obsługuje ponad 1,5 miliona zamówień. Osoby pracujące w centrach logistycznych stanowią fundament naszej działalności, a ich wysiłki pomagają nam w ekspansji naszej firmy na nowe rejony oraz w rozszerzeniu wachlarza świadczonych przez nas usług. Korzystając z najnowszych technologii, stale poszukujemy sposobów na zwiększenie i udoskonalenie gamy oferowanych przez nas produktów – dostarczanych szybko i tanio.
Nasze zespoły w centrach logistycznych są pierwszym ogniwem w łańcuchu dostaw przyczyniającym się do realizacji zamówień klientów w tempie, z którego tak słyniemy. Pracujemy w centrach logistycznych, które stanowią serce prężnej sieci operacyjnej firmy Amazon i określane są niekiedy jako „pierwszy kilometr”, ponieważ to właśnie tutaj większość przesyłek rozpoczyna swoją podróż. Pomagamy również zarządzać dynamicznie zmieniającymi się składami magazynowymi i umożliwiamy realizację szybkich dostaw 24 godziny na dobę.
W naszych centrach logistycznych pracuje wiele różnych osób, bo oferujemy perspektywy dla osób o każdym poziomie umiejętności i wykształcenia. Niektórzy z nas zajmują się bezpośrednio towarami, inni analizują dane, pomagając wszystkim w firmie w podejmowaniu trafnych decyzji.

Minimalne wynagrodzenie zasadnicze dla tego stanowiska jest wskazane poniżej. title: Principal ProServe Cloud Architect, AWS ProServe AGS NAMER
descriptionHtml:
AWS Professional Services (ProServe) is seeking a ProServe Cloud Architect (PCA) specializing in the professional sports and gaming vertical. You will engage directly with organizations such as the NBA, NFL, MLS, NHL, and sports gaming operators to design and deliver cloud solutions tailored to this industry.
As a PCA you operate as the conduit between ProServe Account Executives and Shared Delivery Teams (SDT), ensuring solutions are realistic, achievable, and maximize customer business outcomes (CBOs). You serve as a trusted advisor on industry trends, emerging technologies, and the regulatory landscape.
This is not a role for a sports fan. It requires a professional who understands how leagues operate as businesses: media rights economics, collective bargaining agreements, salary cap structures, franchise revenue models, multi jurisdictional gaming regulations, and how technology underpins live broadcast, fan engagement, and wagering operations. That business fluency, combined with cloud architecture expertise, is what makes this role distinct.
Your success will be measured by SOW signings, successful solution delivery, and customer satisfaction (CSAT).

Key job responsibilities
As an experienced technology professional, you will be responsible for:
• Designing scalable, secure AWS solutions for sports and gaming customers, accounting for real time processing, regulatory compliance, and peak event traffic patterns
• Providing technical guidance during pre-sales and implementation, translating sports business structures (media rights, revenue sharing, franchise economics) into solution architectures
• Collaborating with Account Managers and SDTs to ensure proposals address sports betting compliance (AML, KYC), responsible gaming requirements, and data privacy obligations
• Advising customers on emerging technologies: sports AI/ML, DTC streaming, connected stadium infrastructure, integrity monitoring, and esports platforms
• Sharing knowledge through mentoring, training, and reusable artifacts that capture the regulatory and business patterns unique to this vertical

A day in the life
As a PCA in the sports and gaming vertical, no two days look the same, but your time centers on customers, partners, and solving real problems:
• Engaging directly with customers to understand their cloud journey, identify pain points, and scope solutions that deliver measurable value
• Partnering closely with ProServe Account Executives (PAEs) to align on opportunity strategy, develop statements of work, and drive deals through the pipeline
• Deep diving into customer environments to assess level of effort, define solution architectures, and build business cases that articulate the ProServe value proposition
• Delivering opportunity scoping and solution design focused entirely around the customer, solving their specific problems rather than selling generic services
• Working across organizational boundaries with Solution Architects, Account Executives, and delivery teams both inside ProServe and across the broader AWS sales organization
• Engaging directly with C suite executives, league technology officers, franchise CTOs, and technical experts inside each sports and gaming organization to build trust and drive outcomes

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Sr. Design Program Manager, Worldwide Grocery Real Estate
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Retail Growth & Development (WWRGD) organization is seeking a Sr. Design Program Manager, E-Commerce to lead design and program management across our E-Commerce workstreams for the retail grocery store network. This is a high-impact, individual contributor role requiring deep subject matter expertise in grocery retail design, E-Commerce operational integration, and cross-functional program ownership at scale.

This is an exciting, fast-moving role for a design leader who operates at the intersection of design execution and program leadership. You are the right person for this job if you are a highly independent, detail-oriented design professional who thrives in ambiguity, produces designs that satisfy conflicting interests with a high bar for quality, and can drive alignment across multiple stakeholders with competing priorities.

In this role, you will own the end-to-end design and program coordination for E-Commerce workstreams including but not limited to: E-Commerce Hubs, E-Commerce Metro Optimization, Amazon Counter, and Dash Carts. You will serve as the single-threaded owner and primary point of contact for each business owner, tracking deliverables, managing timelines, and ensuring designs meet strict launch deadlines. You will define the standards and processes to optimize E-Commerce design in retail stores and ensure scalability across the fleet. As the program lead, you will influence decisions across Operations, Technology, Construction, and Procurement.

The ideal candidate is a creative problem solver with strong program management instincts, deep E-Commerce fluency, and the ability to build scalable design systems that work across a high-volume, multi-workstream portfolio.


Key job responsibilities
- E-Commerce Workstream Ownership: Own and drive the full portfolio of E-Commerce design workstreams, serving as the subject matter expert and primary point of contact for business owners.
- Design Execution: Produce design deliverables independently while simultaneously managing the output of others to meet strict launch deadlines.
- Tracking and Reporting: Track and report on the status of all active workstreams, proactively identifying risks, dependencies, and blockers to leadership.
- Cross-Functional Coordination: Collaborate with Operations, Technology, Construction, Procurement, Real Estate, Topology Planning, and senior leadership to align design solutions with business objectives.
- Design Standards and Toolkits: Develop and maintain design standards, templates, and best practices for E-Commerce integration across the grocery store network, enabling consistent and repeatable solutions at scale.
- Program Management: Manage the design process end-to-end, interfacing with internal and external design partners to ensure quality and consistency across all workstreams.
- Site-Specific Adaptation: Adapt site-specific conditions, metrics, and standards to store designs while balancing competing operational, customer experience, and cost requirements.
- Scope Development: Build data-driven scopes of work with internal stakeholders focused on enabling E-Commerce operations within existing and new store environments.
- Design Packages: Create design packages (2/5 page sets) to communicate design intent and program status with cross-functional teams and senior leadership.

title: Sr. Product Manager Technical - AI and Automation, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

As the product owner for AI enablement in this space, you will start by auditing how beta teams work today, mapping workflows, pain points, and repetitive manual tasks to identify the highest-impact opportunities for AI automation or augmentation. You will turn those opportunities into a clear, prioritized roadmap and partner with beta program leads, engineering, and AI teams to build, integrate, and deploy solutions. You will stay current on emerging generative AI models, agentic frameworks, and beta-specific AI tooling, and you will test, evaluate, and benchmark candidate tools against real team use cases to make informed build-versus-adopt recommendations. You will collaborate with the broader Amazon AI and beta communities to surface best practices, reuse existing solutions, and find opportunities to partner. To drive impact, you will lead and document trainings that drive adoption among beta program leads and the wider Experience Validation team.

Key job responsibilities
Success in this role is measured by real, sustained impact on how your beta programs operate. You will establish clear KPIs for adoption and value—active user rates, time saved per task, output quality improvements, and cycle-time reduction—and track them over time to demonstrate ROI and guide your roadmap. You will use data and user feedback to iterate, retire what isn't working, and double down on what is. The ideal candidate is comfortable both exploring emerging AI technology and getting close to operational workflows to understand where the friction really is. You are a self-directed builder who thrives in ambiguity, communicates crisply, and is energized by using AI to help a fast-growing organization do more with less.

descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless opportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. What’s in it for you?
An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Work backwards from the customer, identifying inputs to grow brands and improve their performance across Amazon's retail categories.

title: Quality Assurance Engineer, Community and Fandom - Music
descriptionHtml:
Hundreds of millions of people open Amazon Music to find the artists they love, build playlists that follow them everywhere, and share what they are listening to. The Community & Fandom team owns those social and discovery surfaces, including playlists, artist detail pages, profiles, insights and fan culture features that ship across iOS, Android and Fire Tablet.

We are hiring a Quality Assurance Engineer to help us change how quality gets built here. Our engineering org is moving fast on AI-assisted development, and code generation is no longer the constraint, validation is. That makes this role the leverage point for the entire team, not a downstream checkpoint. You will join at the moment we are doubling QA capacity and rebuilding our approach around automation, so the work you design in your first year becomes the way this org tests for years afterward.

The bugs we care about most are the ones that are hard to find. A playlist that loses a track for one customer in fifty thousand, a race condition that only surfaces on a cold start over a slow network, a memory pattern that degrades after an hour of listening. Finding those before customers do takes engineering judgment, and that is the bar we hire against.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end to end test strategy for features on your surfaces, from test case design through automation coverage and release sign off.
- Build and extend automated UI and integration test suites for Native and shared Kotlin and Compose Multiplatform code running on iOS and Android.
- Work inside our weekly release train, covering branch cut regression, staged rollout validation, and the metrics review that gates dial up to full traffic.
- Investigate low reproduction rate defects using logs, crash and memory telemetry, and weblab side by side comparisons, then turn each finding into a permanent regression test.
- Make accessibility a standing part of feature validation rather than an audit that happens late.
- Partner with our Quality Services team in India, contributing the documented test plans and environments they execute against, and reviewing their results as part of the daily handoff.
- Bring AI-assisted testing into the workflow, using LLM tooling for test case generation, coverage gap analysis, and triage acceleration, and measure whether it actually helps.

A day in the life
You start by reading overnight regression results from the QS team and triaging what changed. A crash signature spiked on the Android beta, so you pull the telemetry, narrow it to a specific playlist size, and reproduce it locally in twenty minutes. You file it with a repro case clear enough that the owning engineer fixes it before lunch. In the afternoon you pair with two SDEs on a new fan culture feature that is a week from branch cut, walking their design for the states nobody thought about yet. You close the day extending the automated suite so the crash you found this morning never ships again.



About the team
Community & Fandom is a mobile and backend org inside Amazon Music Technology. Two of our QAEs are already based in Mexico City, so you will have local peers from day one, and our engineering teams sit in overlapping timezones for real time collaboration. We are growing QA team to help accelerate delivery. We see QA as an integral part of our development flow and we're actively moving to a more deeply integrated QA model.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of quality assurance engineering experience
- Experience in automation testing
- Experience in manual testing
- Experience in UI and API automation testing (Selenium/SOAPUI)
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in API & Mobile testing
- Experience designing and planning test conditions, test scripts, and test data sets to ensure appropriate and adequate coverage and control

Key job responsibilities

title: Engineering Operations Technician, RNO101
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.


Key job responsibilities
Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability

Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)

Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)

Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA

Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment

Technical writing to support change management program

Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion

On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation

Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:

Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:

Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently

Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds

Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder

Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position

Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:

Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

About the team
Our team supports a new machine learning cluster at Amazon, providing the power and cooling that keep thousands of accelerator hosts online around the clock. We are hands-on engineers and technicians who work across electrical, mechanical, and controls disciplines to fix problems and improve how we operate. You will work closely with your peers and site leadership to maintain the systems that enable uninterrupted model training and inference workloads.

Because this cluster is new, you will help build operational processes from the start and grow with the facility over the coming years. There is room to deepen your technical skills, take on process improvement work, and move into more senior roles in critical facility engineering.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance, or 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- vocational/technical training or an associate degree or above, or 4+ years of military experience

descriptionHtml:

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is growing rapidly, and we are looking for Data Center Technician to join our expanding Infrastructure Operations team.
Data Center Operations designs, installs and maintains the world’s largest Computing Infrastructure. Our scope of work includes systems, repairing, dealing with issues, handling and tracking parts and assisting in Data Center maintenance. Amazon Data Centers are large-scale high-density centers where you will help change the face of Technology in the region.


Key job responsibilities
As Data Centre Operations Engineer, you will be the primary point of contact for internal customers. There is never a dull moment as each day presents itself with different challenges. Some of the key responsibilities you will undertake are:

• You will troubleshoot technical issues on advanced hardware, ranging from servers, storage and networking devices on a 24/7 basis.
• You will maintain a high level of system reliability and availability.
• You will participate in projects to enhance operational efficiencies with opportunities to share experiences and knowledge with our global network of technical experts.
• You will share knowledge and help train less technical staff on the best practices related to all service owner issues
• You will contribute towards building a great team by getting involved in the Amazon hiring process/candidate interviews


A day in the life

title: Principal Applied Scientist, Humorphic Labs
descriptionHtml:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Humorphic Labs builds AI systems that work as teammates rather than tools. We ship them six months or more ahead of anyone else. The Lab is small on purpose so it can change direction in a day.

Humorphism concerns the quality of the working relationship between a person and an AI system. It asks whether the system acts proactively adapts to the person and the situation earns trust manages attention and strengthens human judgment. This role turns those behaviors into testable questions then answers them with working systems.

You will own the scientific agenda. You will convert a fuzzy behavioral goal into an end-to-end plan that covers data agent architecture evaluation and the product experiment that tests it. You will write code every week and build large parts of the experimental stack yourself because it does not exist yet.

The first focus areas are agentic products where a domain expert holds judgment the system cannot replace. Amazon Connect places an assistant beside a person handling a live conversation. AWS Bio Discovery places one beside a scientist running experiments. Both need evaluation that measures collaboration quality rather than task completion alone.

The role changes shape as the Lab matures. It starts as hands-on science in close partnership with product and engineering. Later it moves inside a product team to carry adoption of what the Lab proved.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the scientific strategy for human-AI collaboration across agentic and multimodal systems.
• Convert desired interaction behaviors into falsifiable hypotheses evaluation tasks and system requirements.
• Build the evaluation system that measures teammate behavior trust adaptation human contribution and failure recovery.
• Design agent systems that use memory tools planning and recovery then test them with the people who do the work.
• Design data collection and curation for language speech and interaction traces.
• Build significant parts of the experimental stack yourself because that stack does not exist yet.
• Diagnose failures across data models orchestration evaluation and product interaction.
• Define the requirements engineering needs to turn a proven method into a product capability.
• Partner with design product engineering and behavioral research from problem definition through product validation.
• Run experiments with partner product teams then report what worked what failed and what changed as a result.
• Set the standard for reproducible experiments evidence and scientific review inside the Lab.
• Mentor scientists and engineers without moving away from hands-on work.
• Represent the work in internal reviews and in appropriate external scientific venues.

A day in the life
Your week has two centers of gravity.

Most days you build. You take a claim about how a teammate should behave design the smallest experiment that can falsify it and run it. You read interaction traces from real sessions then argue with the engineers about what they mean.

The rest of the week belongs to the people the work is for. You sit with a contact center agent or a bench scientist and watch where the system helps and where it intrudes. You leave with the next hypothesis. Often you leave with evidence that kills the last one.

About the team
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- PhD in computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, or a related technical field, or a Master's degree with equivalent applied science experience, or an equivalent body of work
- Experience developing agentic AI systems or large language model applications through an end-to-end product cycle
- Experience designing evaluation for systems that have no standard benchmark
- Experience writing substantial research or production code in Python or a comparable language
- Experience leading complex scientific work across engineering and product partners
- Evidence of independent decisions in ambiguous, consequential technical environments

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with post-training methods, including supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning
- Experience with multimodal models across language, speech, and vision
- Experience with speech systems or real-time conversational systems
- Experience measuring collaboration quality, trust, adaptation, or human contribution in AI systems
- Experience building agent systems that use memory, tools, planning, and recovery mechanisms
- Experience founding a scientific program, or joining an early team before that team had established its methods
- A record of scientific influence through publications, patents, open-source work, or deployed systems
- Experience mentoring senior scientists and engineers without moving away from hands-on work
- Experience partnering with design, product, and behavioral research from problem definition through product validation
- Experience taking a proven method into a product team and staying until that team adopted it

title: Sr. Software Engineer- AI/ML, Amazon Neuron Training
descriptionHtml:
The Annapurna Labs team at Amazon Web Services (AWS) builds AWS Neuron, the software development kit used to accelerate deep learning and GenAI workloads on AWS Trainium, Amazon's custom machine learning accelerator. Neuron includes an ML compiler, runtime, collectives library, and application framework that integrate with PyTorch and JAX, so customers can train frontier-scale models on Trainium without rewriting their stack.

The Distributed Training team enables the training of a wide range of models, from large-scale pretraining through post-training and reinforcement learning, on AWS's custom ML accelerators. As more customer workloads shift toward RLHF, PPO/GRPO, and other fine-tuning methods, we are building the distributed training infrastructure, parallelism techniques, numerics, and high-performance kernels that these methods depend on. As part of the broader Neuron organization, we work across frameworks, kernels, compiler, runtime, and collectives — a true hardware and software co-design in practice. We not only optimize current performance but also contribute to future architecture designs, since the gaps we characterize today become requirements for the next generation of Trainium.

We are looking for passionate technical leaders who can help us build and fine tune these distributed training solutions. This role offers a rare opportunity to work at the intersection of machine learning, high-performance computing, and distributed systems, where you will help shape the direction of AI acceleration technology.


Key job responsibilities
You will lead the effort to build distributed training and post-training support into PyTorch and JAX for Trainium accelerators. You will work across PyTorch and Neuron software stack with the Neuron compiler and runtime teams to enable and fine tune large-scale training, post training, and reinforcement learning workloads on the latest Trainium instances. You will own the parallelism strategies these models depend on, spanning data, tensor, pipeline, expert, and context parallelism, and apply reduced-precision formats where they measurably pay off. You will profile end to end to determine whether a workload is bound by compute, memory, collectives, or host overhead, then drive the fix to the layer that owns it, working with compiler, runtime, and collectives engineers to land it. You will translate the performance gaps you characterize into requirements that influence frameworks, and contribute upstream to the open source frameworks our customers train on.

About the team
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at Amazon, we embrace our differences. We are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion. We have ten employee-led affinity groups, reaching 40,000 employees in over 190 chapters globally. We have innovative benefit offerings, and host annual and ongoing learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences. Amazon’s culture of inclusion is reinforced within our 16 Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.

Work/Life Balance
Our team puts a high value on work-life balance. It isn’t about how many hours you spend at home or at work; it’s about the flow you establish that brings energy to both parts of your life. We believe striking the right balance between your personal and professional life is critical to life-long happiness and fulfillment. We offer flexibility in working hours and encourage you to find your own balance between your work and personal lives.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team
- Bachelor's degree or above in computer science or equivalent
- * Familiarity with LLM/transformer fundamentals such as attention mechanisms, autoregressive decoding, V-cache behavior, forms of parallelism
- * Experience in machine learning, data mining, information retrieval, statistics or natural language processing

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or above in computer science or equivalent
- Experience in developing and deploying LLMs in production on GPUs, Neuron, TPU or other AI acceleration hardware, or experience in computer architecture
- * Hands-on SFT and/or RLHF/PPO/DPO experience
- * Experience with ML frameworks such as Pytorch/Jax, Distributed libraries and Frameworks, RL frameworks or End-to-end Model Training
- * Experience with performance engineering: workload profiling, characterization (compute bound, memory bound, network bound), and optimization
- * Contribution to open source projects

title: Manufacturing Test Engr Intern, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Lab126 is the research and development team behind Kindle, Fire TV, Echo, Echo Show, Ring and other Amazon devices. Within Lab126, the Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) Manufacturing Test Engineering (MTE) team builds the test systems that verify every device before it reaches a customer. Our stations run on contract manufacturer lines across Asia and North America, and they decide what ships.
MTE is rebuilding factory test around data and AI. We generate test plans with large language models, inspect assemblies with computer vision, and stream every factory measurement into an analytics platform engineers query directly. An intern here works on that platform, not beside it.
You will join a live new product introduction program and own one scoped piece of the factory test solution, from concept through deployment on a production line.


Key job responsibilities
• Write and debug test software (Python, C/C++) for RF, audio, camera, sensor and power test stations
• Build fixtures and bench setups that prove out a new test method before it reaches the line
• Analyze production test data for yield loss, false failures and test time reduction, and quantify what your change recovers
• Run Gauge R&R, correlation and test limit studies for new stations
• Write the test plan your station ships with, and present your results to the team


A day in the life
You start the day with overnight yield and test time data from the factory, then debug a test script or fixture in the lab with your mentor. Afternoons go to a design review with hardware engineers, a DOE on a new sensor test, or a sync with our contract manufacturer team in Asia.
You get a named mentor, a weekly one on one with your manager, and a written project scope on day one. The term closes with a project presentation to AME leadership.


About the team
AME MTE is a global team across Sunnyvale, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hanoi, and we own manufacturing test for the full Amazon Devices portfolio, from first prototype through mass production. Two positions define how we work: a failure that passes on retest is not fixed, and a number that cannot be recomputed is not evidence.

Basic qualifications

- Enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field, with a graduation date after the internship term
- Completed coursework or project work in at least one of: electronics, signal processing, embedded systems, test and measurement
- Programming experience in Python, C#, C++ or MATLAB, and Git based development
- Available for a 12 week internship starting summer, 2027 in Hanoi, Vietnam

Preferred qualifications

- Test automation or instrument control.
- Able to read schematics and work with an oscilloscope, DMM and power supply
- Cpk, Gauge R&R and DOE, and data analysis with pandas, JMP or Minitab
- Exposure to RF, audio or camera test, or to embedded firmware development
- Prior internship, study or research experience in electrical, automation, communication or manufacturing

title: Senior CDR Network Planning Performance Manager, AWS Infra Supply Chain
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Are you ready to architect the digital backbone of tomorrow? We're seeking a CDR Network Plan Performance Manager to drive root cause analysis of build plan misses, identify systemic gaps in planning assumptions, and lead improvement initiatives that raise the bar on plan accuracy and execution reliability. The build plan determines what and how many server racks we can build each week given material and capacity constraints across a 13-week rolling horizon. You will be embedded in this end-to-end process — examining every input and assumption to ensure we are measuring what matters and improving where it counts. As the CDR planning function matures and additional planning elements are introduced (e.g., Landing Plan), the scope of this role will expand accordingly.

The ideal candidate is a data-driven problem solver with deep supply chain or operational planning experience, a relentless curiosity for understanding "why," and the ability to translate analytical findings into actionable process improvements at scale.

Key job responsibilities
Root Cause Analysis & Investigation: Conduct structured root cause analyses (RCAs) on build plan misses — investigating material availability, capacity constraints, vendor delivery, and other inputs that drive the 13-week build horizon. Investigate planning assumptions and inputs to determine where breakdowns occur — distinguishing between data quality issues, process gaps, constraint modeling errors, and execution failures. Document findings with clear causal chains and evidence to support corrective action recommendations.

Performance Measurement & Metrics: Develop and maintain performance metrics that track build plan adherence (racks planned vs. racks built per week), assumption accuracy, and supply chain input reliability. Build dashboards and reporting mechanisms to provide visibility into performance trends, miss categories, and improvement trajectories. Analyze historical performance data to identify recurring patterns, seasonal effects, and systemic vulnerabilities.

Improvement Initiatives: Own and drive improvement initiatives end-to-end — from problem identification through solution design, implementation, and impact measurement. Partner with Build Plan, Landing Plan, Supply Chain, and Engineering teams to implement process changes that address identified root causes. Develop business cases for improvement investments and track ROI of completed initiatives.

A day in the life
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence:

- Work across organizational boundaries to gather data, validate hypotheses, and drive alignment on corrective actions.

- Present findings and recommendations to senior leadership, translating complex analyses into clear narratives.

- Participate in planning forums and reviews, representing the performance perspective and advocating for data-driven decision making.

Process & Framework Development:

- Contribute to the development of performance management frameworks, RCA methodologies, and miss categorization taxonomies.

- Identify opportunities to automate performance tracking and anomaly detection across the build plan cycle.

- Document best practices and develop playbooks for recurring analysis patterns.

- As new planning elements (e.g., Landing Plan) are introduced to CDR, extend performance frameworks to cover the expanded scope.

title: Data Centre Operations Manager, Data Center Operations
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.


Key job responsibilities
About You:
You will have previous management experience, managing teams of high performers.
You will have the ability to refine and develop processes to optimise operational excellence in every area of your role.
You will be able to drive performance levels to achieve the pace we build and operate our Data Centres.
You will have previous experience in Data Centres, either building or managing (or both) along with exposure to developing great relationships with both internal teams and external vendors.

You will also have a passion for technology along with a desire to be the best at your job every day!

About The Role:
As a Data Center Manager in Amazon Web Services AWS, you will get to manage the world’s largest Cloud Computing Infrastructure. We encounter interesting, challenging & complex problems every day, being a technical manager in AWS means that you can innovate to solve these issues and help drive Operations Excellence in all areas of your role.

A day in the life

Your day job will include (but not limited to):

Managing and developing teams of engineers, providing both technical and leadership expertise and ensuring highest levels of performance.
Maintaining existing co-located and in-house Data Centres
Helping build and bring online new Data Centres
Constantly improving all our processes and procedures. We believe there is nothing we cannot improve
Assisting & managing relationships with external vendors & contractors
Liaising with internal teams & management groups
Ensuring we adhere to and exceed local Health & Safety standards in all our Data Centres
Creating and maintaining metrics on all aspects of our Data Centres and utilising those metrics to drive positive changes
Assisting in implementing service methodologies including incident management, problem management, change management, capacity management, etc.

What are we looking for in a successful AWS Data Centre Manager (DCM) candidate along with the technical knowledge and experience?

People Management.
As a successful candidate you will have managed a team of at least 5 individuals, over a period of at least 3 years. You will be able to demonstrate how you have continued to improve performance of an existing team along with displaying skills in creating or growing a team. Experience managing both high & low performing employees will be of advantage along with conflict management.

Incident Management.
You will have a lot of experience dealing with high severity situations, show a clear understanding of the wider blast implications of any issue/outage and potential consequences of differing outcome scenarios. You will also have experience in Change Management & Fault Management.

Vendor Management.
An Amazon, the DCM has to deal with vendors, contractors & security companies. You will be able to prove you have experience dealing with partners and be able to display incidents of both problem & conflict management when dealing with same.

Process Improvement.
You will be able to demonstrate an ability of taking both a good working process & a bad process and improving. You will have experience in processes mapping, implementing remediation steps and how this affected the overall business you were working in. Experience in Kaizen/Lean/Six Sigma is preferable

Health & Safety.
Health & Safety should be at the forefront of every DCMs mind. Managers should be able to positively influence the Safety culture of the Data Centre organization.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
