title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.
We are seeking experienced Engineering Operations Technicians to join our data center operations team, specifically focusing on liquid cooling infrastructure and water distribution systems. This role is vital in maintaining the continuous operation of our advanced cooling systems that support critical data center operations.
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.
NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.


Key job responsibilities
• Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety, and cooling equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
• Monitor and operate mission critical liquid cooling infrastructure
• Conduct glycol concentration testing and adjustments
• Operate and maintain water distribution systems, including water chemistry, pumps and piping networks
• Perform maintenance, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of liquid cooling systems
• Technical writing to support change management program
• Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
• On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
• Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts are usually 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined day, mid, or night schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations. Must be flexible on work schedule and willing to work holidays and weekends, as needed
• Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
• Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
• Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
• Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
• Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
• Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection
This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.
Essential Requirements:
• Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
• Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
• Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility
Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.


A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- 2+ years of electrical and mechanical experience and/or industrial water distribution systems.
- Ability to work on a flexible schedule including days, nights, and/or weekends.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working in a data center or mission critical facility (example: hospital, military facility, public safety facility, etc.)
- Industrial-scale chiller plant operation
- Primary/Secondary loop systems
- Plate and frame heat exchanger maintenance

title: Software Development Engineer, Edgelink ML, Amazon Traffic Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Every second, billions of signals flow in from browsers and edge services around the world. Trails turns that firehose into live, trustworthy data at the point where traffic first meets Amazon. When something goes wrong, or someone is trying to abuse the system, the pipelines you build are how teams see it first.

Trails is a unified edge observability platform. We bring client-side and edge telemetry into one governed data lake, with fine-grained access control built in. Streaming applications deliver live data to downstream detection, mitigation, and traffic insight systems, where latency is measured in seconds, not hours. You will own the data those real-time decisions depend on, and your work will show up quickly in how teams resolve real incidents. Our tools include automated traffic intelligence reports, guided investigation workflows, and dashboards that builders across the company rely on. You will make queries over huge datasets dramatically faster and build the self-serve interface that lets teams investigate traffic patterns on their own. The platform is young, so you will have real say in architecture and direction while solving hard problems in ingestion, data quality, and low-latency delivery.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and ship streaming pipelines and telemetry features for real-time ingestion and observability at scale.
- Optimize and speed up data queries over large datasets through better data layout, partitioning, and query design.
- Build a self-serve interface that lets teams investigate traffic patterns without needing engineering help.
- Build data solutions that make edge systems easier to see, understand, and operate.
- Automate away toil and expand self-serve data query capabilities.
- Power insight reports that help teams triage availability issues and abuse incidents fast.
- Write clean, maintainable code that keeps the platform stable.
- Partner with other teams to bring in new telemetry sources and delight customers.
- Join the on-call rotation to keep the platform available 24x7.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Senior Manager, Human Resources Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Why this role exists
When an Amazonian needs time away for their health, a new baby, or a family emergency, the experience we give them lands at the most vulnerable moments of their working life. Our obligation: do not make a hard (or delightful) moment harder. This leader owns that obligation end to end — the whole experience of taking a leave, across every channel the employee and their manager touch, from the first "I need time" to the return to work.
This role sits inside the single-threaded, obligation-based Leaves model reporting through Business Enablement and Employee Experience. You own the experience obligation; the partner pillar, Business Enablement, owns the data, visibility, defect, and business-case layer. The seam between you is deliberate and defined — the employee never experiences it.

What you own
The end-to-end leave experience across channels — the experience employees, managers, and HR partners have across self-service, chat, and HR/manager-assisted support, and the experience of back-office service delivery (owned operationally by Service Operations; you own how it feels, not how it is run). You own what it feels like to navigate a leave end to end. The employee should experience one Leaves function with one answer — never routed between teams, never handed a confusing message at a sensitive moment.

Proactive and reactive communications and content — chat replies, letters, notifications, and in-the-moment messaging. You own whether an employee understands what is happening to them and why. You deliver these experiences through platform and channel capabilities.

The experience priorities, and the truth behind them — Leave post-resolution review (PRR), contacts per leave case, self-service and deflection, and the experience of each journey step. You own not just the metrics but the causation behind them: you search for what actually drives the number, separate signal from noise, and are persistent about fixing root causes rather than symptoms.
Additionally, you own the experience signal and the standard; the underlying data and system of record sit with Business Enablement, which you consume and inform.

The experience standard — you publish the bar for intake, tone, clarity, and resolution that service, product, and compliance design against. Your deliverable is the standard others build to, not an opinion they consult.

How you operate — a forward-deployed, AI-native builder
This is a non-tech builder role. You and your team are forward-deployed into the employee's actual experience — combining deep customer empathy with the ability to build. You treat customer discovery as the work, not a precursor to it: you spend real time in the lived experiences of employees, managers, and People Experience and Technology (PXT) partners, and you turn what you learn into shipped improvements, working directly with product, tech, service operations, and compliance.

Customer-focused first — you start from the employee and the line leader, not the system. You go the extra mile to understand an experience escalation, make it intuitive and customer-centric, and clearly separate what we own from root causes that sit elsewhere — and own the pen to influence dependency prioritization.

Build on the platform, don't wait for it — you use the available AI and platform capabilities to make experiences real at speed. You reach for the mechanism before the headcount.

Domain-builder bench — you lead and grow a team of domain builders: today's deep experts, upskilled to build directly on our tools, immediately shifting how we deliver for our customers.

Route signal back — the experience defects you find feed the product and compliance interfaces, so each fix hardens the system that produced it.

What success looks like
A truly representative, end-to-end measure of the leave experience that matches what the employee, manager, and line PXT actually goes through, not a set of disconnected stage metrics.

PRR and contacts-per-case moving because root causes are fixed — not because surge capacity is masking them.

Managers and employees stop being redirected for questions they shouldn't have to ask and answers they should have in the moment.

A domain-builder team that ships experience improvements directly, in partnership with product and tech.

Who this is for
A Senior Manager-level, customer-focused builder who is energized by owning an experience no one has owned whole before; who treats time in the customer's reality as the job; who can hold a clear, humane standard for the most vulnerable moments of working life; and who builds — with AI as the default leverage — rather than admires the problem. You would rather ship an improvement an employee can feel this month than produce a plan about it. You hold the line that the complexity is ours to absorb, never the customer's to broker.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 7+ years leading employee-experience, CX, or program functions, including people leadership
- Track record owning an end-to-end customer/employee experience and the metrics behind it
- Experience shipping improvements in partnership with product/tech teams
- Fluency building with AI/automation as primary leverage

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in leave/benefits, HR, or a regulated employee-facing domain
- History of setting experience standards that other teams design against

title: Senior Applied Scientist, Fauna
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an Senior Applied Scientist to lead the development of evaluation frameworks and data collection protocols for robotic capabilities. In this role, you will focus on designing how we measure, stress-test, and improve robot behavior across a wide range of real-world tasks. Your work will play a critical role in shaping how policies are validated and how high-quality datasets are generated to accelerate system performance.
You will operate at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and human-in-the-loop systems, building the infrastructure and methodologies that connect teleoperation, evaluation, and learning. This includes developing evaluation policies, defining task structures, and contributing to operator-facing interfaces that enable scalable and reliable data collection.
The ideal candidate is highly experimental, systems-oriented, and comfortable working across software, robotics, and data pipelines, with a strong focus on turning ambiguous capability goals into measurable and actionable evaluation systems.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and implement evaluation frameworks to measure robot capabilities across structured tasks, edge cases, and real-world scenarios
- Develop task definitions, success criteria, and benchmarking methodologies that enable consistent and reproducible evaluation of policies
- Create and refine data collection protocols that generate high-quality, task-relevant datasets aligned with model development needs
- Build and iterate on teleoperation workflows and operator interfaces to support efficient, reliable, and scalable data collection
- Analyze evaluation results and collected data to identify performance gaps, failure modes, and opportunities for targeted data collection
- Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate evaluation tooling, logging systems, and data pipelines into the broader robotics stack
- Stay current with advances in robotics, evaluation methodologies, and human-in-the-loop learning to continuously improve internal approaches
- Lead technical projects from conception through production deployment
- Mentor junior scientists and engineers

About the team
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.
We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.
Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.
At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.
If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you.

Basic qualifications

- PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
- Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing

Preferred qualifications

- Experience using Unix/Linux
- Experience in professional software development

A day in the life
Deine Aufgabe als Instandhaltungsplaner:in ist der reibungslose Ablauf unserer Operations. Du arbeitest vor Ort in einem unserer Logistikzentren, trägst die Verantwortung für das Management von Anlagegütern und planst die vorbeugende Wartung. Du führst eingehende Analysen unserer logistischen Leistung durch, setzt hohe Standards und optimierst die bestehenden Geräte.

In enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem technischen Team am Standort stellst Du sicher, dass Wartungs- und Reparaturaufträge von Maschinenkomponenten bis hin zu ganzen Systemen entsprechend ihrer Priorität abgearbeitet werden. Du suchst in Kollaboration mit anderen Mitgliedern unseres EU-weiten Netzwerks fortwährend neue, innovative Möglichkeiten zur Effizienzsteigerung.

About the team
Unser Wartungs- und Instandhaltungsteam (Reliability Maintenance Engineering Team oder RME-Team) sorgt dafür, dass unsere Geräte und Ausstattung jederzeit optimal funktionieren. Wir sind ein Team von Techniker:innen und Ingenieur:innen, das aus hervorragenden Teamplayern besteht und von erfahrenen Führungskräften geleitet wird. Wir arbeiten gemeinsam daran, die Geräte in unserem gesamten globalen Netzwerk von Fulfillment-Centern zu warten, zu reparieren und ihre Fehler zu beheben. Einige unserer Mitarbeiter:innen sind Führungskräfte, die das Team bei der Arbeit an spannender, innovativer Technologie beaufsichtigen – die es teilweise nur bei Amazon gibt.
Von der Installation automatisierter Verpackungssysteme bis hin zur Beaufsichtigung der allgemeinen Wartungsarbeiten eines Standorts sowie der Reparatur von für den Vertrieb wesentlichen Geräten wickelt unser Team einen Großteil der technischen Aufgaben bei Amazon ab. Unter anderem sorgt es auch dafür, dass Gebäude weiterhin den rechtlichen Auflagen entsprechen, damit alle sicher bleiben und unsere Standorte mit maximaler Effizienz betrieben werden. Es gibt zahlreiche Aufstiegschancen im RME-Team selbst ebenso wie im gesamten Amazon-Unternehmen.
Alle unsere Aktivitäten sind darauf ausgerichtet, die Ausfallzeiten an Amazons wichtigsten Betriebsstandorten zu reduzieren, damit Kund:innen ihre Bestellungen rechtzeitig erhalten. Oft arbeiten wir früh morgens, spät abends oder in der Nachtschicht, um Wartungsarbeiten mit den geringstmöglichen Störungen vorzunehmen. Falls wir eine bessere Möglichkeit finden, eine bestimmte Aufgabe zu erledigen, verfügen wir über die Fertigkeiten und Gelegenheiten, vollständig neue Prozesse oder bahnbrechende Technologie wie Amazon Robotics oder unseren Complex Item Sorter einzuführen.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager
descriptionHtml:
OpenSearch is growing fast, and we need a Technical Program Manager who can keep pace. In this role, you will drive feature releases, coordinate security and compliance campaigns, and remove cross-team blockers so engineers can focus on building great products.

You will own program strategy end-to-end — planning roadmaps, aligning engineering and business stakeholders, and making informed trade-offs that keep delivery on track. Your ability to bring structure to ambiguity and connect the work of multiple teams will directly accelerate what OpenSearch delivers to its customers.

Key job responsibilities

About the team
The OpenSearch team builds and maintains open-source search and analytics technology used by customers worldwide. title: Software Engineer, Worldwide Amazon Stores Finance Technology, Controllership Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's finance teams rely on financial controls to keep spending accurate and financial reports audit-ready. You will build the systems that automate those controls, catch errors and waste before money is spent, and give finance analysts fast, trusted answers through AI tools built on cloud services and large-scale data.

Key job responsibilities
- Build services that check purchase requests and orders against finance rules in near real time, then correct or flag issues before approval.
- Automate financial controls, such as reviews of fixed assets, leases, cost centers, open orders, so finance teams spend less time collecting data by hand and more time acting on exceptions.
- Build data pipelines on AWS, including Lambda, StepFunctions, Glue, EMR, DDB, and S3, that feed C-Hub/dashboards finance teams use during month-end close and audit reviews.
- Build AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with the Strands SDK, including MCP tools, context and memory management, evaluation, harnesses, and guardrails that keep finance answers accurate.
- Big data experience with Spark, StarRocks, or similar OLAP engines.
- Build web applications and browser extensions in React and TypeScript that let finance users review exceptions, filter large datasets, and export results.
- Turn defined business requirements into technical designs, review them with senior engineers, and take them from prototype to production.
- Own your services in production. Write the tests, alarms, and automated rollbacks that let a change reach customers in hours, not days. Take part in on-call rotation.
- Work directly with finance, accounting, product, and data science partners, and explain technical tradeoffs.

A day in the life
Most of your day goes to building. You might start by looking into an alarm from an overnight data job that feeds a finance control. Then you meet an accounting partner to design how a manual review could run automatically. After lunch, you write code and tests and ship the change through an automated pipeline the same day. Some weeks, you test a new AI model against an evaluation set to see if it gives better answers. Near month-end close, you answer finance users who want to know why a control flagged a transaction.

About the team
We are a team of software engineers who build the tools that keep Amazon's spending accurate and its financial reports audit-ready. Our customers are finance analysts, accountants, and employees across Amazon who buy goods and services. We own our products end to end, from data pipelines and services to the web apps and AI agents people use every day. We ship changes through automated pipelines and measure our work by the manual effort and errors we remove. We value clear writing, careful reviews, and engineers who ask why a process exists before they automate it.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Knowledge of machine learning model architecture and inference
- Knowledge of computer architecture, operating systems, and parallel computing
- Knowledge of professional software engineering & best practices for full software development life cycle, including coding standards, software architectures, code reviews, source control management, continuous deployments, testing, and operational excellence

descriptionHtml:
Build the technology that makes delivery faster and more reliable for millions of customers across Europe. Lead delivery and customer experience for EU Easy Ship, one of Amazon’s fastest-growing fulfillment programs.

As a Product Manager – Technical, you will set the vision and strategy for capabilities that support Easy Ship’s path to becoming the standard for seller fulfilled orders at Amazon. With scope across EU marketplaces, you will connect customer needs with technology investments and shape how this growing business earns customer trust. The role offers ownership of a significant product area and the opportunity to influence its direction as the program expands.

The applicable collective agreement for this role is CBA for employees of Telecommunication Sector. The position is classified at level 7, depending on the candidate's skills, competences and experience.

Key job responsibilities
Define and execute the product roadmap, including new fulfillment modes, expanded eligible selection, and carrier integrations.
Own end-to-end delivery promise accuracy across EU marketplaces, reducing missed commitments and unnecessarily conservative delivery dates.
Translate customer needs into detailed requirements and partner with engineering to evaluate designs and launch scalable features that reduce delivery defects.
Negotiate carrier promise parameters that balance competitive delivery speeds with achievable service commitments.
Establish success metrics and analyze weekly performance, explaining gaps, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions.
Use data-driven outreach and targeted interventions to improve carrier and seller compliance with shipping requirements.
Align sponsors, Technical Program Managers, and multiple development teams to deliver complex initiatives and resolve dependencies.
Manage competing priorities and resource trade-offs, directing investment toward the greatest customer and business impact.
Create, maintain, and share project plans, milestones, decisions, and progress updates with stakeholders.
Identify, assess, track, and mitigate risks and issues; anticipate bottlenecks, manage escalations, and balance business needs with technical constraints.

A day in the life
Your day will combine customer insights, technical product development, and collaboration across Europe. You’ll review delivery performance, investigate missed promises, and work with engineers to define features that improve speed and reliability. You’ll meet with worldwide Easy Ship product teams and EU stakeholders to prioritize the roadmap, resolve dependencies, and prepare launches. Conversations with carrier partners will focus on delivery commitments and integration improvements. You’ll also write product requirements and assess launch results, keeping customer needs central to decisions while building scalable capabilities that support Prime eligibility and help sellers deliver orders reliably to millions of customers across EU marketplaces.

About the team
The EU Easy Ship team is part of EU External Fulfillment and one of Amazon's fastest-scaling programs, designed to give MFN Sellers a seamless, end-to-end logistics experience. Amazon manages the entire supply chain from seller warehouse pick-up to customer doorstep delivery. Sellers simply pick, pack, and confirm pickup or drop-off. Amazon selects the optimal carrier and ship method at promise generation. The result: sellers see measurable sales uplift through faster delivery promises, improved unit economics via competitive shipping rates, and peace of mind from built-in customer claim protection. By joining this team, you will help shape a program that is transforming how thousands of sellers fulfill orders and how millions of customers experience delivery.

- Experience working effectively on milestone-driven projects
- Experience working cross functionally with tech teams

- Experience working with data analytics and using these metrics to identify problems, or experience in customer acquisition

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in e-commerce, retail or advertising, or experience in logistics
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

title: Sr Technical Business Development Manager, Talent Markets, AWS Forward Deployed Engineering
locations: East Palo Alto, CA, United States
descriptionHtml:
AWS is seeking a Sr. Technical Business Development Manager to own the go-to-market strategy that gives a fast-growing forward deployed engineering (FDE) organization durable access to the engineers it needs to grow. Forward deployed engineers pair deep production software experience with direct customer engagement: they work alongside customers to solve complex technical problems, build production solutions, and turn emerging technology into scalable outcomes. The market for this talent is specialized and competitive, and winning in it requires a deliberate strategy, real investment, and subject matter fluency in the work itself.

You will own that strategy end to end. You will build a fact-based view of the talent market, define where AWS should compete and invest, and develop the business cases, investment proposals, and executive narratives that fund and direct that work. You will structure and manage a portfolio of external relationships, with technical communities, professional networks, industry groups, and conference organizations, as channels that give AWS credible access to experienced engineers. You will carry measurable goals for qualified pipeline, orchestrate delivery across engineering, marketing, communications, events, finance, legal, and Talent Acquisition without direct authority, and use market and conversion data to decide where to expand, redirect, or exit. You own the strategy and the business outcome; partner teams run execution and operations, and Talent Acquisition owns candidate outreach, assessment, and hiring at the downstream hand-off.

This role requires technical fluency in forward deployed engineering and the AI and cloud landscape, strong business judgment, and the ability to create clarity in an ambiguous environment where strategy, plan, and stakeholders are not predefined. You will advise senior leaders, negotiate and structure external engagements, and align teams you do not own. Travel: 30 to 50%.

Key job responsibilities
Own the go-to-market strategy for building durable access to forward deployed engineering talent. Translate the organization's growth plans and engineering needs into where AWS competes, which segments to prioritize, and how to allocate investment.

Build a fact-based view of the talent market: concentration, candidate motivations, competitive dynamics, geography, and emerging sources of qualified engineers.

Develop the external value proposition for FDE opportunities at AWS, grounded in technical credibility with experienced engineering audiences.

Build business cases, investment proposals, and operating plans for new pipeline initiatives, and carry the goals and performance measures that judge their return.

Structure and manage a portfolio of external relationships (technical communities, professional networks, industry groups, conference organizations) as channels for reaching relevant engineers. Negotiate the terms and model of AWS participation.

Orchestrate delivery across engineering, marketing, communications, events, finance, legal, operations, and Talent Acquisition, owning the business outcome while partner teams run execution.

Establish the mechanisms that connect external engagement to the recruiting process: shared goals, pipeline attribution, feedback loops, and operating rhythms with partner teams.

Measure market reach, audience quality, qualified pipeline, program efficiency, and conversion. Recommend where AWS should expand, redirect, replicate, or discontinue investment.

Identify repeatable, scalable approaches that extend across technical disciplines, markets, and business teams while holding AWS's quality bar.

Advise senior leaders on market position, pipeline strategy, investment requirements, and risks to the growth plan. Represent AWS credibly with technical leaders, engineering communities, and executive audiences.

A day in the life
Your work centers on how AWS builds sustained access to the specialized talent forward deployed engineering depends on. You will work with FDE leaders to understand growth plans, technical priorities, and future capability needs, then translate those into a market strategy, an investment thesis, and a portfolio of initiatives. Much of the role is strategic and deal-oriented: you might decide AWS should compete in a specific engineering community, build the business case for a flagship initiative around an emerging discipline, and negotiate the terms of AWS's participation with an external organization. You will define the audience and business outcome, secure investment, align contributors across the org, and set the goals and quality bar, while partner teams handle delivery and logistics. You will track portfolio performance and shifts in the AI and engineering talent market, use pipeline and conversion insight to see which markets and initiatives produce the strongest return, and advise senior leaders on opportunities, investment choices, and risks. Success is whether your strategy creates a scalable, durable source of qualified forward deployed engineering talent.

About the team

title: Sr. Creative Designer, Amazon Customer Service
descriptionHtml:
Customer experience is at the heart of all we do at Amazon, as we strive to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Amazon Customer Service (CS) is at the forefront of customer experience, working relentlessly to provide customers a convenient, high-quality, and delightful experience across all of our channels, in every interaction.

Internally, behind every critical leadership moment, campaign, and program that connects CS employees worldwide, there is a Creative & Marketing team turning strategy into engaging experiences. We are hiring a Sr. Creative Designer to join the Creative & Marketing team within Org Enablement.

This role leads the creative direction and production of video, motion graphics, and live event experiences that drive engagement and connection across Amazon Customer Service. You will partner with communications strategists, learning designers, and program managers to translate organizational priorities into compelling visual content, from leadership videos and engagement and learning campaigns to on-location event production.

In this role, you will concept, direct, produce, and deliver work from start to finish, making brand and creative trade-off decisions along the way. The ideal candidate brings strong skills across camera production, video editing, and motion design in After Effects, and thrives in a fast-paced environment. You will co-create briefs and creative direction with stakeholders as the subject matter expert, and you will design compelling creative proposals to drive engagement with critical CS priorities and programs. You will use your judgment to move work forward when objectives are broad, timelines are shifting, or stakeholder needs are still forming.

Application Requirement: Online portfolio demonstrating motion graphics, video production, and event design work.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead creative direction for CS and Org Enablement programs at the initiative level. Co-create briefs with stakeholders, develop creative proposals, and execute the content or experience. Direct the creative output of internal partners so every deliverable connects to campaign objectives and business outcomes. Synthesize research, stakeholder feedback, and performance data into insights that shape future content.

- Own video production end to end, in the studio and on location. Produce content for leadership communications, live events, campaigns, and learning experiences. Work across the creative stage (creative pitches, concept, storyboard, script, art direction) and the production and post production stage (camera, lighting, audio, editing, and motion design in Adobe After Effects and Premiere Pro, and tools such as Vyond and Synthesia).

- Lead event design and production of live leadership moments such as Town Halls and summits. Work across creative disciplines and with cross-functional partners from early concept and stage design through on-site capture, audio and visual setup, and post-event delivery.

- Build scalable creative systems. Develop motion design templates and integrate AI tools into creative workflows to drive efficiencies and keep the brand complaint and consistent at scale.

- Hold a high creative bar. Make sound creative decisions in ambiguous, fast-changing environments while maintaining brand and quality standards. Influence senior stakeholders without direct authority, and fully commit to decisions once they are made.

- Operate with production discipline. Build workback plans that account for stakeholder review cycles, manage several projects at once, and mentor team members on motion and video best practices.

A day in the life
You start the day at the team stand-up, reviewing priorities and new requests in the project queue. After stand-up, you might direct a leadership message shoot in the studio. You set up the camera, lighting, and audio, coach the speaker on delivery, and capture several takes. In the afternoon, you could be editing a video for an campaign or learning program and incorporating feedback from a recent stakeholder review.

Many briefs start out broad, so you often help shape them. You meet with communications and learning partners to define what success looks like, then come back with a creative proposal and storyboard that show how the work will meet that goal. Between projects, you build templates that help the team move faster, try AI enhancements with creative tools, and share what you learn with junior designers. Some weeks include travel for live events, where you handle stage design, audiovisual setup, and on-site filming, then see the work through to post-event delivery.

About the team
The Creative & Marketing team, part of Org Enablement, operates as an internal creative and content agency for Amazon Customer Service. Our mission is to turn CS priorities into experiences that help employees understand, stay informed and connect with the CS vision.

We partner with stakeholders across CS from the first brief through final delivery. Every project starts with strategy. We define the audience, the message, and the channels that will reach them. We then bring that strategy to life through creative direction, visual design, motion graphics, video, live events, and campaigns built to scale. We also maintain the CS brand and the templates and tools that help leaders communicate with their teams across the globe.

We work alongside communications, learning design, program management, and product teams to create content that builds connection and engagement across organization.

We're a high-performing creative team that values customer obsession, innovation, and trusted partnerships with our stakeholders across CS.

If you love building creative work that brings a global organization together, we'd love to hear from you.

Basic qualifications

- Experience with asset management, design workflows, or partnering with creative teams
- 4+ years of experience in motion design, video production, or visual design, with a comprehensive portfolio.
- Proficient with Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects and Premiere Pro) Figma, and Microsoft products (like Outlook, SharePoint, PowerPoint).
- Experience in video production, live streaming technologies (including stage design, audio/visual setup), studio workflows, edit and post- production techniques, and production planning.
- Experience working cross-team and synthesizing feedback and/or performance data (metric tests, research studies), to steer the direction of future creative content.
- Experience in creating content and experiences for internal communications and leadership development, including live events, Town Halls, and multi-channel campaigns.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in driving compelling creative strategy and execution at an agency or in-house creative team
- A degree or certification in graphic design, mass communication, film production, or equivalent.
- Experience with Creative tools such as Vyond, Synthesia.
- Experience with accessibility standards and implementation.
- Knowledge of AI-assisted creative tools and workflows.
- Experience prioritizing and handling multiple assignments at any given time while maintaining commitment to deadlines.
- Experience communicating complex information and solutions to senior stakeholders and influencing decisions.
- Experience as a subject-matter expert in one or more design disciplines, supporting teams, solving creative challenges, and mentoring emerging designers.

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Network Product Development, Interconnects
descriptionHtml:
AWS builds one of the largest networks in the world, and every rack that lands in a data center depends on optics, copper, fiber and switches all arriving on time. The Network Product Development (NPD) Interconnects team designs and brings to production the optical modules, DAC/AEC copper cables and structured fiber that connect AWS infrastructure.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help drive how our products move from forecast to factory to data center. You will be the day-to-day interface between Supply Chain, our manufacturing vendors and the NPD engineers who design our products. You make sure each group has the technical context, data and decisions it needs from the others. When a forecast changes, a supplier raises a constraint or a build stalls, you bring the right people together quickly, frame the trade-offs clearly and drive the issue to resolution.

We work quickly and practically. Rather than waiting for large software programs, you will use AI tools, agents, scripts and lightweight workflows to stand up working processes fast. You'll run them on a regular cadence with our partners and improve them as you learn. Once a process has proven itself, you will help turn it into durable tooling.

Key job responsibilities
- Drive the end-to-end program for interconnect products (optical modules, DAC/AEC, fiber and structured cabling) from forecast to delivery, and report progress and risks to NPD and Networking leadership through a regular business review.
- Act as the primary interface between Supply Chain, vendors and NPD engineering. Translate engineering constraints into supply implications and supply constraints into engineering decisions.
- Coordinate technical review of significant forecast changes (product mix or volume) with engineering and Supply Chain before they are shared with suppliers.
- Help keep long-range capacity commitments and short-range build signals distinct. Raise it early when an execution signal risks undoing a long-lead commitment (DSPs, lasers, PCBs, raw fiber materials, line capacity).
- Partner with engineering and Supply Chain to keep BOM and allocation data consistent, so sub-tier requirements line up across commodity managers.
- Run scenario analyses (for example a 50% demand increase or decrease) with Supply Chain and engineering to show where commitments break across components and sub-tiers, and help teams agree on the response.
- Work with vendors and Supply Chain to track supplier commitments and de-commitments for critical sub-tier parts
- Drive a weekly clear-to-build (CTB) review with vendors and Supply Chain that combines component availability against the build plan, escalates shortfalls early and handles excess inventory without stopping the line.
- Track capacity KPIs with our vendors. Work with engineering and site teams to validate capacity constraints when the data doesn't line up.
- Coordinate with Supply Chain and deployment teams on inventory at VMI hubs and rack integrators, so production plans reflect where finished units can actually go.
- Support rack integration improvements with engineering and integrators: rack portfolio standardization, production-readiness validation for new rack designs, first-pass yield, test time and the time from PO to start of assembly.
- Use AI tools and agents every day to automate data gathering, reconcile vendor and Supply Chain data, generate status reports and catch issues early.
- Build AI-assisted workflows that cut manual spreadsheet work for engineers and Supply Chain partners, and share what works across the team.
- Write requirements and work with software teams to turn proven processes and AI-assisted workflows into durable tools.

A day in the life
Your week might start with a CTB review across optics and fiber vendors, where an AI agent you set up has already reconciled the latest vendor data and flagged a laser shortfall weeks ahead. You then pull Supply Chain and engineering together to work through what a forecast revision means for supplier agreements. Later you follow up with a vendor on a capacity constraint that doesn't match their reported output, and join a call with a rack integrator on why a high-volume configuration keeps failing first-pass test. You write clear updates for leadership and turn this week's manual fixes into next week's automated workflow. Expect regular travel between Seattle and the Bay Area, as well as to supplier and integrator sites, mostly in Asia.

About the team
NPD Interconnects handles product development for the optics, copper and fiber that link AWS networks, from early engineering through NPI and volume production. We work closely with the NPD switch and software teams, Global Supply Management, fabric and deployment teams, and our manufacturing partners worldwide. We value strong partnerships, mechanisms over good intentions, and a "trust, but verify" approach to the data we rely on.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Bachelor's degree in Operations, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or another technical field
- Experience working with large-scale data mining and reporting tools (i.e. SQL, MS Power Query, Python), or experience delivering forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis, and data interpretation of results
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- 5+ years of experience in hardware supply chain, manufacturing operations, or NPI for electronic, optical, or networking products
- Experience working directly with ODMs, JDMs, or contract manufacturers on capacity, CTB, or production ramps

Preferred qualifications

- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership
- Master's degree or above in Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or Business Administration, or Master's degree or above in engineering, statistics, computer science, operations research, business analytics, information systems or equivalent
- Experience communicating and presenting to senior leadership
- Experience leveraging AI-powered tools or data analytics platforms to drive quality improvements, root cause analysis, or process optimization
- Experience using AI-powered or data-driven scheduling and planning tools to optimize maintenance workflows
- Experience with optical transceivers, DSP and laser supply, copper interconnects, or fiber cabling manufacturing
- Experience with multi-tier BOMs, allocation, or sub-tier supply visibility for long-lead components
- Experience with rack-level integration and test, yield improvement, or design for manufacturability

title: Security Engineer II, Customer Service Security
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to protect customers at a global scale while seeing the direct impact of your work? The Customer Service Security team at Amazon is looking for a Systems Security Engineer who thrives in ambiguity and is passionate about engineering solutions that reduce security risk across customer service operations. With billions of customer contacts per year spanning more than 40 countries, the security challenges here are complex and the stakes are real.

In this role, you will partner directly with business teams to identify security risks, design pragmatic controls, and build solutions that simultaneously improve security outcomes, customer experiences, and associate experiences. You will own security architecture decisions, lead risk mitigation discussions, and construct frameworks that enable others to apply your work in a repeatable way. If you are a self-starter who can navigate undefined problems and turn them into scalable security solutions, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead security reviews, threat modeling, and risk assessments for customer service systems, identifying pragmatic approaches to mitigate risks while enabling teams to launch securely.
- Design and build security controls and engineering solutions that protect customer data and empower secure customer contacts at scale.
- Partner with business stakeholders, product owners, and engineering teams to understand emerging risks and define security strategies where none yet exist.
- Create security frameworks, runbooks, and rubrics for new problem domains that enable other engineers to apply consistent, repeatable security practices.
- Communicate security risk and design decisions clearly in writing to both technical and non-technical audiences, and mentor other security engineers on best practices.

A day in the life
You will operate independently, engaging directly with business and engineering teams to uncover security risks that do not come with predefined solutions. On a given day you might be conducting a threat model for a new customer contact workflow, writing a security framework that other teams will adopt, or reviewing architecture proposals to ensure they meet the security bar. Much of your time is spent navigating ambiguity — translating business context into concrete security requirements and building the path forward. You will balance proactive roadmap-driven work with responding to emerging security concerns as they arise.

About the team
The CS Security team is dedicated to reducing security risk across Amazon's customer service organization. We engineer solutions that keep customer data secure while enabling fast, high-quality customer and associate experiences at massive scale. Our work touches billions of customer contacts annually across more than 40 countries, giving you the opportunity to build relationships across the company and scale your solutions globally. We are investing in new engineering capabilities to make every customer contact more secure, and this is an exciting time to join as we shape that future.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of programming in Python, Ruby, Go, Swift, Java, .Net, C++ or similar object oriented language experience
- 2+ years of scripting, programming, and security code review in a common programming language (non-internship) experience
- 2+ years of troubleshooting systems issues, analyzing logs, or automating basic tasks using command line tools (non-internship) experience
- Bachelor's degree in a STEM field (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics), or 2+ years of IT Security experience
- Knowledge of networking protocols such as HTTP, DNS and TCP/IP
- Knowledge of industry-based security vulnerabilities and remediation techniques
- Experience in troubleshooting systems issues, analyzing logs, or automating basic tasks using command line tools (non-internship experience)

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of command line tools to troubleshoot protocols, analyze log outputs, or automate basic tasks
- Experience performing security activities across one or more phases of the software development lifecycle (SDLC), such as security design review, threat modeling, secure code review, and security testing

title: Senior Customer Sucess Manager , Time Bound Account Management (TBAM)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s 3P Seller Business is one of the fastest-growing segments in e-commerce, and the Time Bound Account Management (TBAM) team is at the center of defining how that growth reaches unmanaged sellers. We’re looking for a Senior Customer Success Manager III who will drive seller outcomes across TBAM’s 155K+ US unmanaged seller population by combining exceptional discovery and seller intelligence with intentional, scalable engagement strategies. This role operates across two core pillars: deep seller understanding and scaled outreach.

You’ll manage a significant seller portfolio, conducting high-quality discovery conversations that surface the real challenges and opportunities within each seller’s business. You’ll extrapolate key themes across your pipeline to identify patterns, build seller intelligence that informs how the team prioritizes and targets, and use those insights to shape scalable engagement approaches. Equally, you’ll design and operate within scaled outreach mechanisms—leveraging AI tools and prioritization frameworks to drive coverage across a large population, test engagement strategies, and measure what moves sellers to action.

The combination of these two pillars is what makes this role unique: your discovery work generates the intelligence that makes scaled outreach effective, and your scaled outreach surfaces the signals that tell you where to go deep. You’ll continuously iterate between the two, feeding learnings into cross-functional roadmaps and shaping seller targeting logic across the broader TBAM organization and partner teams.

This role demands someone who leads with curiosity and seller advocacy, can navigate high ambiguity, deliver independently with limited guidance, and drive strategy with senior stakeholders across Amazon to drive outcomes that impact the US 3P store. You’ll drive organizational process improvements, develop scalable best practices, and represent the voice of the unmanaged seller in strategic planning forums.

You bring a customer-first mindset, you’re fluent in data, and you can translate seller-level insights into marketplace-level strategy. A bachelor’s degree is required.


Key job responsibilities
Lead discovery and seller intelligence across your portfolio—conduct high-quality discovery conversations that surface seller challenges, growth opportunities, and operational pain points. Extrapolate key themes across your pipeline to build a strategic picture of your population, identify what drives seller action, and generate insights that inform how the team prioritizes engagement across the broader unmanaged seller pool.
Drive scaled outreach with intentional use of AI and data—leverage scoring models, prioritization frameworks, and tracking mechanisms to execute engagement at scale across your portfolio. Test outreach approaches, measure effectiveness in real time, and iterate on what’s working versus what needs to change. Approach AI with intentionality, using it to accelerate your ability to reach and serve sellers while maintaining the human judgment that makes outreach effective.
Manage a large seller portfolio with strategic precision—balance high-touch engagements on complex supply chain, category, or business strategy topics where your domain expertise and coaching drive seller action with scaled mechanisms that maintain coverage across your broader population. Use discovery insights to inform where you go deep and scaled signals to identify where to investigate further.
Package learnings into scalable assets—identify patterns across your seller conversations and portfolio data, convert insights into repeatable playbooks and frameworks the broader TBAM team can adopt, and drive process improvements that eliminate friction and create predictable, repeatable paths for the organization.
Drive strategy with stakeholders—own the narrative on what’s working across both discovery and scaled engagement, present data-backed recommendations to senior leaders across multiple orgs, shape seller targeting logic across the 155K+ unmanaged seller pool, and represent the voice of the unmanaged seller in cross-functional forums.


A day in the life
As a CSM III, your day moves fluidly between deep seller engagement and scaled outreach. You might start by reviewing AI-driven scoring outputs and portfolio prioritization to plan your outreach strategy, then shift into seller conversations where you’re going deep on supply chain challenges, category opportunities, or growth blockers. These discovery calls are where you build trust, uncover the real issues, and coach sellers toward action. Between engagements, you’re analyzing patterns across your pipeline—what themes keep emerging, what’s driving seller action, and where your scaled approaches are gaining traction. You’ll use AI tools intentionally to track engagement effectiveness, surface emerging trends, and determine where to test new outreach strategies. You’ll regularly drive strategy sessions with senior stakeholders across partner teams, presenting findings from both your discovery work and scaled experiments to shape how the team approaches the unmanaged population. You’ll also drive process improvements that eliminate friction for the full TBAM team and prep strategic recommendations for leadership on what to test next.

About the team
As a member of TBAM, you will collaborate closely with our Supply Chain and Category teams as well as Strategic Account Services (SAS), driving FBA adoption, supply chain optimization, and category growth for US 3P unmanaged sellers. You’ll be part of a ~40-person TBAM organization that rewards autonomy, intellectual curiosity, and a bias for action. We operate as domain experts who influence, coach, and guide seller behavior—and we’re hiring people who want to raise that bar even further.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
- Experience communicating and presenting to senior leadership
- 7+ years of experience in customer success management, enterprise account management, sales strategy, or consultative client-facing roles
- Experience leveraging AI tools, automation, or data-driven workflows to scale customer engagement and drive business outcomes
- Demonstrated ability to operate across discovery-based engagement and scaled outreach models, with a focus on iterating based on data and seller insights
- Experience managing large client or seller portfolios requiring strategic prioritization and high-quality relationship management
- Proficiency in data analysis and comfort building narratives from data

Preferred qualifications

- Experience identifying patterns across customer or seller conversations and translating qualitative insights into scalable strategies
- Familiarity with Amazon Seller Central, FBA operations, or 3P marketplace dynamics
- Experience using prioritization frameworks, scoring models, or tracking tools (SQL, QuickSight, Tableau, or similar) to manage portfolio coverage
- Track record of translating qualitative customer/seller insights into quantitative business cases that shape product or program roadmaps
- Experience partnering cross-functionally with product, engineering, or automation teams to inform how manual processes can be scaled
- Track record of identifying process inefficiencies, diagnosing root causes, and implementing scalable solutions

title: Front-End Engineer II, AWS Agentic WorkSpaces -  WorkSpaces Admin and Builder CX
descriptionHtml:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Do you want to build the agentic experiences that millions of administrators rely on to run their cloud desktops? The AWS WorkSpaces Forefront team is reinventing how customers discover, onboard, and manage WorkSpaces by embedding generative AI directly into our consoles and SDK. As a Front End Engineer, you will build the customer-facing surfaces of our agentic harness — the always-on platform layer that hosts our LLM agents: a streaming conversational surface where admins ask questions and get grounded answers, agentic wizards (Quick Setup, Create WorkSpace, catalog management) where the agent recommends and the customer confirms, and the feedback and telemetry that turn every interaction into signal for our ranking and evaluation systems. These surfaces ship in the WorkSpaces Console on a shared platform that powers AI experiences across multiple WorkSpaces products, and you'll build and own features on it alongside a team of strong engineers.

We are a fungible mix of front-end, back-end, and ML/AI engineers driving higher customer conversion through AI-powered onboarding, building a suite of AI capabilities into our consoles — LLM agents, personalization, recommendations, and experimentation — and unifying our platform at the architectural level. On the front end, that means rendering streamed agent responses and tool-call progress in real time, designing human-in-the-loop confirmation flows for agents that act on a customer's behalf, building bounded-choice wizards that collapse a dozen decisions into one guided path, and instrumenting conversion funnels and A/B experiments so we can prove each change is better for customers. Our consoles are built in TypeScript and React on Cloudscape (the AWS design system) and are moving toward a federated console architecture.

At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. As a Front End Engineer II, you'll own features end to end — from UX collaboration and design through implementation, testing, launch, and operation — on surfaces that directly move customer conversion. You'll work alongside senior engineers on the harder, more ambiguous problems, participate in design and code reviews, and partner with UX designers, applied scientists, and backend engineers to bring agentic experiences to customers. Because the harness is a multi-product platform, what you build is reused by every team shipping AI experiences on it.

Key job responsibilities
Build the conversational and agentic wizard surfaces of the harness — streaming chat UI, tool-call and progress rendering, result cards, and human-in-the-loop confirmation and hand-off flows — in TypeScript/React on Cloudscape in the WorkSpaces Console.



Build guided onboarding and provisioning experiences (Quick Setup, Create WorkSpace, catalog management) where the agent recommends and the customer confirms, with clear paths back to the full console for everything else.



Instrument the customer journey end to end — feedback capture, recommendation acceptance, funnel events — and build the front-end side of our A/B experimentation, so agent quality and conversion are measured, not guessed.



Help define the front-end contract with the harness backend: typed interfaces for agent responses, tool results, and streaming, co-designed with backend engineers so new expert agents render correctly without bespoke UI work.



Deliver accessible (WCAG), localized, and performant experiences — streaming latency, bundle size, perceived responsiveness — and share in operational excellence for the console surfaces (availability, client-side error monitoring, on-call readiness).



Contribute reusable components and patterns to the shared platform and to our federated console architecture so product teams can build agentic surfaces consistently.



Write well-tested, maintainable code; participate in design and code reviews; and help onboard new engineers and interns.



A day in the life
You might spend the morning building the streaming response renderer for a new expert agent and wiring its confirmation step, pair with a UX designer at midday to iterate on the Create WorkSpace recommendation card against customer feedback, and in the afternoon add funnel instrumentation and read out an A/B experiment with an applied scientist — then ship it behind a feature flag. You'll operate in an agile environment where development cycles are measured in weeks, see your work reach customers quickly, and learn from senior engineers tackling the hardest parts of the platform.

WorkSpaces Forefront owns the admin experience across the WorkSpaces Consoles (Personal, Applications) and the WorkSpaces SDK. We're building an agentic control plane for Console and programmatic experiences — an agentic harness (LLM agents, routing, ranking, personalization, memory, knowledge bases, MCP tools, and evaluation) plus experimentation and closed-loop learning — while unifying key infrastructure toward a federated console architecture.

About the team
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. title: Program Manager II - Devices Beta, Amazon Devices Beta
descriptionHtml:
The Amazon Devices Beta (ADB) Team is your hall pass to play at work!! We are responsible for the “real world validation” for Kindle eReaders, Fire Tablets, FireTV products, and Emerging products…think, Amazon Smart Oven and Amazon Basics Microwave. How do we do this? By playing with these products every day! We work with product and engineering teams to prepare new product launches, system software and app updates, and marketplace expansions. Our goal is to gather feedback and expose issues and bugs prior to the product launching, so we delight our customers with products beyond their expectations.

Key job responsibilities
The ADB Team needs an experienced Program Manager to help us build and execute programs to validate the customer experience during the product development cycle. You will work with end users and a wide variety of internal teams to develop the strategy and execute the program to confirm from a customer perspective we are ready to launch. You will be a “hands on” contributor to support and troubleshoot issues, resolve problems, and keep the feedback flowing. Along the way, you’ll identify opportunities for improvements and put processes and tools in place to help us scale. You will track, communicate status, and independently drive issues to resolution. Cross-team coordination, program management, and an ability to learn and understand new technologies are essential.

A day in the life
Our programs are global and composed of Amazon employees across the company. We put pre-released devices and/or software in the hands of beta testers who represent our target customer profile ("people all about smart home automation", "people who love to read", or "people who are native speakers of French"). Working with our product team counterparts, we ask testers for “no holds barred” feedback to tell us what works and what needs to be fixed. Our bar is always being raised and we strive to achieve an Amazon 4-Star or better product every time!

About the team

title: Sr. Learning Designer - Technical Training, RME Learning Experience
descriptionHtml:
The Reliability and Maintenance Engineering (RME) team keeps Amazon's fulfillment network running. Our technicians, engineers, and maintenance leaders are builders, problem-solvers, and operators who take ownership of the systems our customers depend on, operating 24/7 to deliver uptime, equipment reliability, safety, and quality. As the network grows and becomes more complex, our workforce needs training that makes the complex simple and puts the right knowledge in their hands at the right moment.

We're reshaping our learning function, rethinking how one of the largest engineering workforces in the world learns. If you want to help build what comes next, come join us.

RME Learning Experience (RLX) is looking for a Sr. Learning Designer with deep experience creating content for technical training to design and deliver learning experiences that grow capability across RME's engineering workforce.

You will design learning that makes complex technical content accessible, durable, and applicable in a live, 24/7 operations environment where safety and speed both matter. Your work will span the full spectrum of RME's technical workforce: technicians building foundational skills, engineers deepening expertise, and career changers entering engineering for the first time.

Your experience creating technical training content will allow you to translate complex engineering concepts into structured, effective learning experiences. You will take programs from needs analysis through design, development, and scaled delivery, building content that drives genuine behavior change and measurable skill development.

You will integrate AI into learning design and delivery, using AI-augmented analysis, design, and development to streamline launch times and focus effort on high-value creative work.

You will build the case for design decisions using learning science and data-driven analysis, and bring stakeholders along through evidence and clear communication.

Key job responsibilities
- Design technical training content that builds real capability. Translate complex engineering processes, systems, and procedures into structured learning experiences grounded in learning science and instructional design best practices.
- Apply multiple modalities to technical content. Design across formats (eLearning, simulation, hands-on labs, job aids, blended programs) selecting the right approach based on the complexity of the technical content and the context in which it will be applied.
- Design for transfer, not just knowledge. Build learning that closes the gap between knowing and doing, ensuring technicians and engineers can apply what they learn in real operational conditions where safety is non-negotiable.
- Partner with SMEs to ensure technical accuracy and relevance. Build strong working relationships with engineers and technical leaders to ensure content reflects current systems, standards, and operational realities.
- Build scalable, maintainable content architectures. Design content structures, templates, and standards that allow technical training to scale across regions, site types, and operating models without losing accuracy or effectiveness.
- Integrate AI into the design and development process. Use AI-augmented tools to accelerate content development, streamline review cycles, and focus effort on the design decisions that require human judgment.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Instructional Design, Educational Technology, Technical Training, Design, or a related field
- Experience in a training role, including technical training
- Experience in training, performance management and coaching/mentoring
- Experience developing or delivering training programs across multiple sites or regions

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or equivalent in Education, Instructional Design, or a related field
- Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification
- Experience with graphic training systems, multimedia content creation, and Learning Management Systems (LMS) administration
- Experience leading training strategy initiatives across large-scale operations and working cross-functionally at senior levels
- Experience mentoring trainers, using data analytics for training effectiveness measurement, and leading change management initiatives
- Experience with predictive and preventative maintenance, repair, troubleshooting, and diagnostics on material handling equipment (MHE) and automated conveyor systems

As the Senior Regional Automation Engineer, you will engage on all aspects of high-level support for the control systems within a region of Amazon sites.
